task_instance: Given a sample project tracker export (10 tickets across 3 owners, with statuses/priorities/due dates/notes) for a fictional 'Platform Engineering' team, generate a weekly leadership status report following the skill's exact output template (Executive Summary, Overall Status, Key Metrics, Accomplishments, In Progress, Risks and Issues, Decisions Needed, Next Period Priorities), deriving the metrics (completion rate, overdue count, high-priority open count) from the raw data with a script rather than inventing them.
evidence: Created project_tracker_export.csv (10 sample tickets) in the work directory to stand in for a project-tracker connector export (no connectors are available offline, which the skill itself anticipates via its 'If Connectors Available' section -- degrading gracefully to manual data is expected behavior). Wrote analyze.py and ran `python3 analyze.py`, which computed: 3/10 done (30% completion), 1 overdue item (Rate limiting for public API, 5 days late), 4 open high-priority items. Used these real computed figures (not invented ones) to populate status_report.md, following the skill's Output template verbatim section-by-section. Verified the deliverable with a grep check confirming all 8 required section headers (Executive Summary, Overall Status, Key Metrics, Accomplishments This Period, In Progress, Risks and Issues, Decisions Needed, Next Period Priorities) are present in status_report.md, and manually reviewed that table rows/metrics match the source CSV and the analyze.py output (e.g. the overdue item and its owner/notes carry through into the Risks and Issues and In Progress tables). No network access, connectors, or uninstalled tools were needed -- the core deliverable (a written, data-grounded status report) is a pure text-generation task achievable fully offline with python3/csv and a text editor.
